To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a palladium-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate addition of an arylboronic acid to an enal was developed to form a highly substituted quaternary stereogenic center with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivity.

the enantioselectivity of a palladium(0) (S)-pyridinooxacazoline-catalyzed conjugate addition was improved by the use of para-alkoxy-substituted arene, and that this method was successfully applied to a formal synthesis of (+) -dichroanones and (+)-tawaniaquinone H.
the palladium-catalyzed conjugate addition of arylboronic acids to α,β-unsaturated ketones is highly enantio-, regio-, and diastereoselective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new synthetic methods, and the application of these methods to the total synthesis of natural products.
the design and synthesis of new chiral ligands and their application in asymmetric catalytic reactions.

the development of a catalytic asymmetric formal synthesis of the biologically active (+)-dichorone and (+)-taiwaniaquinone H that features the first enantioselectivie conjugate addition of an aryl Grignard reagent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has provided an elegant and concise catalytic, enantiomerically selective route to (+)-dichoranoone and (+)-taiwaniaquinone H.
the catalytic enantioselectivity of this reaction was not as good as it could be, but it is still a good example of the power of catalytic enantiospecificity.
the catalytic, enantioceroselective formal synthesis of the natural products (+)-dichoranone and (+)-tauaniaquinone H was achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a new palladium(II)-based catalyst in a highly enantiodivergent conjugate addition allowed for the synthesis of two structurally distinct natural products.
we have developed a new catalytic enantioselectivie route to the all-carbon quartenary stereocenter, which is a challenging task.
a palladium(III) intermediate, which was formed by a ligand-assisted oxidative addition, was the key to the enantioselectivity of the conjugate addition reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hammett constant of an aryl group can be used to estimate the relative reactivity of an aryl-substituted substrate for asymmetric conjugate addition.
a combination of a new substrate and a novel bicyclic intermediate allowed us to complete the formal synthesis of (+/-)-dichroaanthone and (+/-)-taiwanaquinone H.
the Hammett constant is a valuable tool for the rational design of substrates for asymmetric catalysis.
